text:
maria: Quick rundown from the weekend runs — A100 vs H100 on the open-7b workload (prefill=512 / decode=32) across us-east1 / eu-west1. Pulled median (p50) and 95th (p95) for prefill/decode, tokens/sec, and an estimated $/1M tokens using on-demand GPU price assumptions.

maria: Results (summaries first):
```
Model: open-7b (vanilla transformer)
Config: seq_prefill=512, seq_decode=32, batch=1 steady-state

A100 (us-east1, cutlass kernels + fp16 nf4 quant):
  prefill p50: 185ms   p95: 320ms
  decode p50: 9ms      p95: 18ms
  tokens/sec: 1,420
  est $/1M tokens: $13.2

H100 (eu-west1, triton kernels + fp16 nf4 quant):
  prefill p50: 128ms   p95: 220ms
  decode p50: 7ms      p95: 12ms
  tokens/sec: 1,860
  est $/1M tokens: $9.8

Notes: H100 shows ~30% prefill latency reduction and ~25-30% better tokens/sec. Cost delta assumes same rack pricing; results include NVLink memory configs for H100.
```

devon: Which quantization and kernel combos did you run? any fallbacks?

maria: Ran three variants for each GPU: fp16 baseline, nf4/8-bit-perf (our custom NF4 pack), and dynamic int8 (GPTQ-lite). Kernel sets: Cutlass+cuBLAS fallback, Triton attention for H100, and a reference FlashAttention path.

maria: Observed behaviour:
- nf4 on H100 gave best cost/latency.
- int8 sometimes triggered a kernel fallback on A100 for certain shard sizes -> p95 spike (see below).
- For large prefill (512) memory layout matters: A100 needed slightly larger batch packing to keep utilization.

maria: Raw-ish sample log snippet showing fallback on A100:
```
[2026-03-18T03:22:15Z] kernel_select: cutlass_fp16 -> int8_fallback (reason: unsupported layout)
[2026-03-18T03:22:15Z] exec: increased_latency ms=240 path=fallback
```

samir: Nice. For capacity planning — what does this imply for QPS per GPU?

maria: Quick capacity calc (steady-state QPS for user-facing 1-request-at-a-time workloads):
- H100 ~1,860 tok/s, typical request ~544 tokens (512+32) => ~3.4 req/s => ~293s of throughput per GPU-hour? (rough calc)
- That maps to ~3,000 requests per hour per H100 for that profile.
- A100 ~1,420 tok/s -> ~2.6 req/s -> ~2,000 requests/hour.
So H100 gives ~45% more request capacity at this seq profile.

devon: Can you push small-batch batching (B=4) numbers? also which cloud SKU used for the price estimate?

maria: B=4 (amortizes prefill):
- H100 tokens/sec -> ~6,700 tok/s (decode amortized), prefill p50 bumped ~+10% due to scheduling
- A100 tokens/sec -> ~5,300 tok/s, prefill p50 +18%
Price assumptions: on-demand per-hour GPU list (us-east1 A100, eu-west1 H100) + 2x for infra overhead to get $/1M tokens. Exact sheet attached in PR.

perf-bot: job_2123 completed: 24 bench runs, variance <6% across repeats. Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-perf/open-7b/2123456789/

devon: Good. For next steps:
- rerun int8 with layout tweak to avoid cutlass fallback (A100)
- run the same nf4 profile on Llama-2-13B scaled down (to confirm linearity)
- add cross-zone latency check (we saw ~8ms tail net penalty eu->us)

maria: Agreed. I'll queue up the int8 layout experiment and drop the config diff in the bench PR. If no objections, recommend H100 for public hosted tiers where latency/cost matters; A100 still fine for bursty, cheaper reserved capacity contracts. :thumbsup:

samir: +1. Add a short note for onboarding docs about the int8 fallback caveat so infra teams don't unintentionally enable it.

maria: Will do. Follow-up PR with charts and the exact $ assumptions tomorrow.
